title: Carlo Acutis (1991–2006)
hook: a teenager who built a website on Eucharistic miracles, now a canonized saint

segments.voice: Yesterday, Leo the Fourteenth, a friar from Chicago by way of Peru, whose first words were for peace. Your line was peace be with you all.

A teenager in Milan sits at the family computer, teaching himself to code. He isn't building a game. He's building a website. Country by country, he gathers accounts of Eucharistic miracles, stories of the bread and wine of the Mass tied to wonders, and lays them out as panels anyone could print and hang up. The same boy makes silly films with his pets, and rations his own video games so they don't take over. His name was Carlo Acutis, and the Church now calls him a saint.
screen: `A TEENAGER TEACHES HIMSELF TO CODE.` → `A WEBSITE OF EUCHARISTIC MIRACLES.` → `NOW CALLED A SAINT.`

segments.voice: First, the ordinary part. People who knew him remember a boy in jeans and sneakers, good with computers, who stuck up for classmates who were picked on and stopped to talk with homeless people near his home. Second, the website. He believed, as the Catholic Church teaches, that Jesus is truly present in the Eucharist, and he wanted people to notice. So he spent his spare time building an online exhibit of Eucharistic miracles, the way another kid might build a fan site. It has since been printed and shown in parishes far from Milan. Third, his line. Carlo used to say the Eucharist was his highway to heaven, and those around him say he went to Mass whenever he could, every day if possible. The image was a teenager's own; the text behind it is older. In John's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims, Jesus says: "I am the living bread which came down from heaven." As his family tells it, his days were built around that sentence. Fourth, his other remembered saying: everyone is born an original, but many die as photocopies. He died young, of leukemia, offering his suffering, those with him said, for the pope and for the Church. He is buried in Assisi, where pilgrims file past his tomb, and he was canonized together with Pier Giorgio Frassati, another young layman. Carlo didn't flee the internet or drop his friends, some Catholics point out. He used the tools in front of him to point at what he loved.
screen: `AN ORDINARY BOY IN JEANS AND SNEAKERS.` · `A WEBSITE OF EUCHARISTIC MIRACLES.` · `THE EUCHARIST, MY HIGHWAY TO HEAVEN.` · `BORN ORIGINALS, NOT PHOTOCOPIES.` · then, large: `I AM THE LIVING BREAD.`

segments.voice: Picture your phone and the last few things you did on it, no guilt, just noticing, then choose one small good thing it could be for: a kind message, a true and beautiful thing shared, a search for a food bank or a parish near you. If you pray, offer your screen time to God the way Carlo offered his; if you don't, let this minute be quiet and unscrolled.
Carlo Acutis. A teenager from Milan who built a website on Eucharistic miracles, called the Eucharist his highway to heaven, and is now honored as a saint.
